answer: Age in the trust hierarchy is bought with per-identity verified output rather than with elapsed time, so an operator cannot batch his accounts through a queue and must run each one through genuine, individually verified work. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. Picture a jade verified individually, a willow who has no stake in the farm, and a whisper earned by both: skipping the jade means skipping the willow, and without the willow there is no whisper. Each head also needs a stranger to attest that work.
